item.title: Kanagawa at New Year: Kawasaki Daishi, the Hakone Ekiden & a Day-by-Day Plan
item.description: Kanagawa has the busiest New Year in Japan, and most visitors to Tokyo never realise it. Kawasaki Daishi draws around three million worshippers in the first three days of January, putting it among the two or three most-visited temples in the country. Tsurugaoka Hachimangu in Kamakura takes over two million more. And on January 2 and 3, the Hakone Ekiden — the relay race that stops the nation — runs its entire course through this prefecture, from the Kawasaki waterfront to the shore of Lake Ashi and back.

item.title: Hakone Ekiden Guide: New Year Relay Race & Access
item.description: Every January 2nd and 3rd, the nation stops to watch the Hakone Ekiden — the most beloved and dramatic long-distance relay race in Japan. University teams of runners carry a sash (tasuki) over a gruelling ~217 km round-trip course between Tokyo and Hakone, climbing the steep mountain road past Odawara to Lake Ashi and back. The race is a New Year institution, with millions watching on TV and huge crowds lining the route to cheer the young runners through cold, hills and exhaustion.
